jeremiah.name: Jeremiah
jeremiah.role: Prophet who warns Judah and speaks about its return
jeremiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jeremiah.importance: God calls him when he says he is too young to speak. He warns the temple crowd, and Pashhur puts him in stocks. Officials throw him in a pit, and Ebedmelech pulls him out. After the city falls, survivors take him to Egypt.
jeremiah.connections: He is Hilkiah’s son, from the priests of Anathoth. Baruch writes his words, and Judah’s officials jail him.

hilkiah-father.name: Hilkiah, Jeremiah’s father
hilkiah-father.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hilkiah-father.importance: The first verse names him as Jeremiah’s father. He is one of the priests in Anathoth in Benjamin. The book does not say he is the high priest of Josiah’s time.
hilkiah-father.connections: He is Jeremiah’s father and one of the priests in Anathoth.

josiah.name: Josiah
josiah.role: King during the start of Jeremiah’s work
josiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
josiah.importance: God’s word first comes to Jeremiah in his thirteenth year as king. Later Jeremiah reminds Jehoiakim of him. Josiah did what was fair and judged the cause of the poor. Jeremiah says it went well with him then.
josiah.connections: He is Amon’s son. Jehoiakim, Shallum, and Zedekiah are his sons.

amon-king.name: Amon, king of Judah
amon-king.role: Josiah’s father, named in two dates
amon-king.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
amon-king.importance: The book names him only as Josiah’s father. His name appears where the book dates Jeremiah’s first message. He does nothing in this book.

jehoiakim.name: Jehoiakim
jehoiakim.role: King who uses unpaid labor and burns Jeremiah’s scroll
jehoiakim.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehoiakim.importance: Jeremiah says he builds his house with workers he does not pay. He has the prophet Uriah brought back from Egypt and kills him. Jehudi reads him Jeremiah’s scroll. He cuts it up and burns it, though three officials beg him not to.
jehoiakim.connections: He is Josiah’s son and Jehoiachin’s father.

zedekiah.name: Zedekiah, king of Judah
zedekiah.role: King who asks Jeremiah in secret but will not surrender
zedekiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zedekiah.importance: He sends men to ask Jeremiah for help against Babylon. He lets the officials put Jeremiah in a pit, then lets Ebedmelech save him. Jeremiah tells him to give himself up, but he fears being mocked. He runs at night and is caught near Jericho.
zedekiah.connections: He is Josiah’s son, and Hamutal is his mother. Nebuchadnezzar makes him king, then captures and blinds him.

nebuchadnezzar.name: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar.role: Babylonian king whose armies capture Jerusalem
nebuchadnezzar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nebuchadnezzar.importance: God calls him “my servant” and gives the nations into his hand. His army surrounds Jerusalem and breaks in. At Riblah he kills Zedekiah’s sons and puts out Zedekiah’s eyes. The book also says Babylon will be punished in its turn.
nebuchadnezzar.connections: He makes Zedekiah king and later judges him at Riblah. He tells Nebuzaradan to take care of Jeremiah.

jehoiachin.name: Jehoiachin
jehoiachin.role: Judean king taken to Babylon and later released from prison
jehoiachin.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehoiachin.importance: The book also calls him Jeconiah and Coniah. Jeremiah says God will cast him and his mother into another land. Nebuchadnezzar carries him to Babylon. In the thirty-seventh year, Evilmerodach frees him from prison and feeds him each day.
jehoiachin.connections: He is Jehoiakim’s son. His mother and the princes of Judah go to Babylon with him.

jehoahaz-judah.name: Shallum
jehoahaz-judah.role: Josiah’s son who is led away and will not return
jehoahaz-judah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehoahaz-judah.importance: Jeremiah calls him Shallum. He became king after Josiah and then was led away captive. Jeremiah tells the people to weep for him, not for the dead. He will die where he was taken and not see his land again.
jehoahaz-judah.connections: He is Josiah’s son and became king after him.

david.name: David
david.role: Earlier king whose family is promised a fair ruler
david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
david.importance: Jeremiah tells the house of David to do justice every morning. God promises to raise a righteous Branch for David. That king will rule fairly, and Judah will be safe. God says David will never lack a man on the throne.
david.connections: Jeremiah calls Judah’s royal family the house of David.

manasseh-king.name: Manasseh, king of Judah
manasseh-king.role: Earlier king whose acts God blames
manasseh-king.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
manasseh-king.importance: God says he will toss Judah among all the kingdoms. He gives the reason: what Manasseh did in Jerusalem. The verse does not list those acts.
manasseh-king.connections: He is Hezekiah’s son and a king of Judah.

moses.name: Moses
moses.role: Earlier leader God names with Samuel
moses.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
moses.importance: God says he would not turn toward Judah even if Moses stood before him. Moses does nothing else in this book. God names him to show that no one’s plea will help now.

samuel.name: Samuel
samuel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
samuel.importance: God says he would not turn toward Judah even if Samuel stood before him. Samuel does nothing else in this book. His name shows that pleading for Judah will not work now.

rachel.name: Rachel
rachel.role: Mother heard weeping for her children in Ramah
rachel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
rachel.importance: A voice is heard in Ramah. Rachel weeps for her children and will not be comforted, because they are gone. God tells her to stop weeping. He says her children will come back from the enemy’s land.
rachel.connections: The poem calls the lost people her children.

baruch.name: Baruch
baruch.role: Writer who records and reads Jeremiah’s words
baruch.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
baruch.importance: He stores the deeds for Jeremiah’s field in a clay jar. He writes Jeremiah’s words on a scroll and reads it at the temple. After the king burns it, he writes it again. When he complains of sorrow, God promises him his life.
baruch.connections: He is Neriah’s son. He writes for Jeremiah, and Johanan’s group takes both men to Egypt.

pashhur-immer.name: Pashhur, son of Immer
pashhur-immer.role: Temple officer who strikes Jeremiah and puts him in stocks
pashhur-immer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
pashhur-immer.importance: He hears Jeremiah’s warning and strikes him. He locks him in the stocks at the upper gate of Benjamin. The next day he lets him go. Jeremiah gives him a new name, Magormissabib, and says he will die in Babylon.
pashhur-immer.connections: He is the son of Immer the priest. He is not Pashhur the son of Malchijah.

pashhur-malchijah.name: Pashhur, son of Malchijah
pashhur-malchijah.role: Official sent to Jeremiah who later asks for his death
pashhur-malchijah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
pashhur-malchijah.importance: Zedekiah sends him with Zephaniah to ask Jeremiah for God’s help against Babylon. Later he hears Jeremiah tell the people to go out to the Chaldeans. He and three other officials ask the king to put Jeremiah to death.
pashhur-malchijah.connections: He is Malchijah’s son. He is not Pashhur the son of Immer.

zephaniah-priest.name: Zephaniah, the priest
zephaniah-priest.role: Priest who carries the king’s requests to Jeremiah
zephaniah-priest.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zephaniah-priest.importance: Zedekiah sends him to Jeremiah twice, once to ask for help and once for prayer. Shemaiah writes to him and asks why he has not punished Jeremiah. Zephaniah reads that letter to Jeremiah. After the city falls, Nebuzaradan takes him to Riblah.
zephaniah-priest.connections: He is Maaseiah’s son and the second priest. The king of Babylon kills him at Riblah.

hananiah-azzur.name: Hananiah, son of Azzur
hananiah-azzur.role: Prophet who says Babylon’s rule will end in two years
hananiah-azzur.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hananiah-azzur.importance: He says God will bring back the temple vessels and the captives within two years. He takes the wooden bar off Jeremiah’s neck and breaks it. Jeremiah tells him God did not send him and he will die that year. He dies in the seventh month.
hananiah-azzur.connections: He is Azzur’s son, from Gibeon. He speaks against Jeremiah in the temple.

uriah-shemaiah.name: Uriah, son of Shemaiah
uriah-shemaiah.role: Prophet killed for warnings like Jeremiah’s
uriah-shemaiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
uriah-shemaiah.importance: He speaks against the city and the land, as Jeremiah does. Jehoiakim wants him dead, so he flees to Egypt. The king’s men bring him back. Jehoiakim kills him with the sword and throws his body among the common graves.
uriah-shemaiah.connections: He is Shemaiah’s son, from Kiriath Jearim. Jehoiakim sends Elnathan to bring him back from Egypt.

micah-prophet.name: Micah, the Morashtite
micah-prophet.role: Earlier prophet whose warning helps defend Jeremiah
micah-prophet.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
micah-prophet.importance: Some elders quote him at Jeremiah’s hearing. Micah said Zion would be plowed like a field. Hezekiah did not kill him for it. The elders use this to argue that Jeremiah should live.
micah-prophet.connections: He spoke in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah.

hezekiah.name: Hezekiah
hezekiah.role: Earlier king recalled for hearing Micah’s warning
hezekiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hezekiah.importance: The elders recall how he heard Micah’s warning. He did not put Micah to death. He feared the LORD and asked for his favor, and the disaster did not come. The elders set this beside the call to kill Jeremiah.
hezekiah.connections: Micah spoke in his days. Manasseh is named as his son.

ahikam.name: Ahikam
ahikam.role: Official who keeps Jeremiah from being killed
ahikam.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahikam.importance: The crowd at the temple wants Jeremiah dead. Ahikam stands with Jeremiah, so he is not handed over to the people. Later the book names him as the father of Gedaliah.
ahikam.connections: He is Shaphan’s son and Gedaliah’s father.

shaphan.name: Shaphan
shaphan.role: Father of several officials who help Jeremiah
shaphan.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shaphan.importance: Shaphan does nothing himself in this book. His son Ahikam protects Jeremiah. His son Elasah carries Jeremiah’s letter to Babylon. Baruch reads the scroll in the room of his son Gemariah.
shaphan.connections: Ahikam, Elasah, and Gemariah are named as his sons. Gedaliah and Micaiah are his grandsons.

elnathan-achbor.name: Elnathan, son of Achbor
elnathan-achbor.role: Official who brings Uriah back and later defends the scroll
elnathan-achbor.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
elnathan-achbor.importance: Jehoiakim sends him to Egypt with men to bring back Uriah. Uriah is then killed. Later he hears Baruch read the scroll. He begs the king not to burn it, but the king does not listen.
elnathan-achbor.connections: He is Achbor’s son. He serves King Jehoiakim.

elasah-shaphan.name: Elasah, son of Shaphan
elasah-shaphan.role: Messenger who carries Jeremiah’s letter to Babylon
elasah-shaphan.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
elasah-shaphan.importance: Zedekiah sends him to Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon. He carries Jeremiah’s letter to the captives there. The letter tells them to build houses and plant gardens. He appears only in this verse.
elasah-shaphan.connections: He is Shaphan’s son. He travels with Gemariah the son of Hilkiah.

gemariah-hilkiah.name: Gemariah, son of Hilkiah
gemariah-hilkiah.role: Messenger who helps carry Jeremiah’s letter to Babylon
gemariah-hilkiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
gemariah-hilkiah.importance: Zedekiah sends him to Babylon with Elasah. The two carry Jeremiah’s letter to the captives. The text does not say which Hilkiah is his father.
gemariah-hilkiah.connections: He is Hilkiah’s son. He is not Gemariah the son of Shaphan.

ahab-kolaiah.name: Ahab, son of Kolaiah
ahab-kolaiah.role: Prophet in Babylon whom Jeremiah says lies
ahab-kolaiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahab-kolaiah.importance: Jeremiah’s letter says he tells lies in God’s name. It also charges him with adultery with his neighbors’ wives. God will hand him to Nebuchadnezzar, who will kill him in front of the captives. The captives will use his name in a curse.
ahab-kolaiah.connections: He is Kolaiah’s son. Jeremiah names him beside Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah.

zedekiah-maaseiah.name: Zedekiah, son of Maaseiah
zedekiah-maaseiah.role: Prophet in Babylon whom Jeremiah says lies
zedekiah-maaseiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zedekiah-maaseiah.importance: Jeremiah’s letter names him with Ahab as a lying prophet in Babylon. It charges both with adultery with their neighbors’ wives. God will hand them to Nebuchadnezzar to be killed. A curse will recall that the king roasted them in the fire.
zedekiah-maaseiah.connections: He is Maaseiah’s son. He is not King Zedekiah.

shemaiah-nehelamite.name: Shemaiah, the Nehelamite
shemaiah-nehelamite.role: Man in Babylon who writes to have Jeremiah punished
shemaiah-nehelamite.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shemaiah-nehelamite.importance: He hears Jeremiah’s message that the captivity will be long. He writes to Zephaniah and asks why Jeremiah is not in the stocks. Jeremiah answers that God did not send Shemaiah. None of his family will see the good God will do.
shemaiah-nehelamite.connections: He writes to Zephaniah the priest and to the people in Jerusalem.

hanamel.name: Hanamel
hanamel.role: Jeremiah’s cousin who offers him a field in Anathoth
hanamel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hanamel.importance: He comes to Jeremiah in the court of the guard. He asks Jeremiah to buy his field in Anathoth. Jeremiah pays seventeen shekels of silver and signs the deed. God says houses and fields will be bought in this land again.
hanamel.connections: He is the son of Shallum, Jeremiah’s uncle.

rechabites.name: The Rechabites
rechabites.role: Family who will not drink wine
rechabites.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
rechabites.importance: Jeremiah brings them to a temple room and sets wine before them. They refuse, because Jonadab told them never to drink wine. They also live in tents, as he said. God sets them beside Judah, who has not listened to him.
rechabites.connections: They call Jonadab the son of Rechab their father. Jaazaniah is named with them.

jaazaniah-rechabite.name: Jaazaniah, the Rechabite
jaazaniah-rechabite.role: Rechabite whom Jeremiah brings to the temple
jaazaniah-rechabite.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jaazaniah-rechabite.importance: Jeremiah takes him, his brothers, and his sons to the temple. The whole house of the Rechabites comes too. The text names him first but gives him no words of his own.
jaazaniah-rechabite.connections: He is the son of another Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah.

jehonadab.name: Jonadab
jehonadab.role: Father whose rules the Rechabites keep
jehonadab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehonadab.importance: He told his family never to drink wine. He told them to build no houses and to live in tents. In Jeremiah’s day they still obey. God promises that Jonadab will always have a man to stand before him.
jehonadab.connections: He is Rechab’s son. The Rechabites call him their father.

gemariah-shaphan.name: Gemariah, son of Shaphan
gemariah-shaphan.role: Official whose temple room Baruch reads in
gemariah-shaphan.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
gemariah-shaphan.importance: Baruch reads the scroll to the people in his room at the temple. His son Micaiah tells the officials what he heard. Gemariah hears the scroll with them. He begs the king not to burn it, but the king will not listen.
gemariah-shaphan.connections: He is the son of Shaphan the scribe. Micaiah is his son.

micaiah-gemariah.name: Micaiah, son of Gemariah
micaiah-gemariah.role: Listener who tells the officials what Baruch read
micaiah-gemariah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
micaiah-gemariah.importance: He hears Baruch read the scroll at the temple. He goes down to the king’s house and tells the officials. They send for Baruch, and the scroll reaches the king.
micaiah-gemariah.connections: He is the son of Gemariah and the grandson of Shaphan.

elishama-scribe.name: Elishama, the scribe
elishama-scribe.role: Scribe whose room holds the scroll
elishama-scribe.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
elishama-scribe.importance: He is with the officials when Micaiah brings news of the scroll. They hear Baruch read it. They leave the scroll in his room and go to tell the king. Jehudi takes it from there to read to the king.
elishama-scribe.connections: He sits with the officials who hear Baruch.

delaiah-shemaiah.name: Delaiah, son of Shemaiah
delaiah-shemaiah.role: Official who asks the king not to burn the scroll
delaiah-shemaiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
delaiah-shemaiah.importance: He sits with the officials who hear Baruch read the scroll. They tell Baruch and Jeremiah to hide. He asks the king not to burn the scroll. The king does not listen.
delaiah-shemaiah.connections: He is Shemaiah’s son. He joins Elnathan and Gemariah in asking the king.

zedekiah-hananiah.name: Zedekiah, son of Hananiah
zedekiah-hananiah.role: Official who sits with the princes in the scribe’s room
zedekiah-hananiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zedekiah-hananiah.importance: He sits with the officials when Micaiah reports Baruch’s reading. The text names him once and gives him no act of his own.
zedekiah-hananiah.connections: He is Hananiah’s son. He is not King Zedekiah.

jehudi.name: Jehudi
jehudi.role: Messenger who reads the scroll to Jehoiakim
jehudi.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehudi.importance: The officials send him to bring Baruch and the scroll. Later the king sends him to get the scroll from Elishama’s room. He reads three or four columns to the king. The king cuts the scroll and burns it all.
jehudi.connections: He is the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi.

arrest-officers.name: The officers sent to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch
arrest-officers.role: Three men the king sends to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch
arrest-officers.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
arrest-officers.importance: After he burns the scroll, Jehoiakim tells these three to seize Baruch and Jeremiah. They do not find them. The text says the LORD hid them.
arrest-officers.connections: Jerahmeel is called the king’s son. Seraiah is Azriel’s son, and Shelemiah is Abdeel’s son.

jehucal-shelemiah.name: Jehucal
jehucal-shelemiah.role: Official who asks for prayer and later for Jeremiah’s death
jehucal-shelemiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehucal-shelemiah.importance: Zedekiah sends him to ask Jeremiah to pray for the people. Later he hears Jeremiah tell the people to go out to the Chaldeans. He joins the officials who ask the king to kill Jeremiah. The text spells his name Jehucal and Jucal.
jehucal-shelemiah.connections: He is Shelemiah’s son. Zedekiah sends him with Zephaniah the priest.

irijah.name: Irijah
irijah.role: Guard captain who arrests Jeremiah at the gate
irijah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
irijah.importance: He stops Jeremiah at Benjamin’s gate and says he is going over to the Chaldeans. Jeremiah says that is false. Irijah does not listen and takes him to the officials. They beat Jeremiah and put him in prison.
irijah.connections: He is the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah.

jonathan-scribe.name: Jonathan, the scribe
jonathan-scribe.role: Scribe whose house becomes Jeremiah’s prison
jonathan-scribe.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jonathan-scribe.importance: The officials make his house the prison and put Jeremiah in its cells. Jeremiah stays there many days. He begs Zedekiah not to send him back, or he will die there. Jonathan himself does not act or speak.
jonathan-scribe.connections: The text calls him the scribe. He is not Jonathan the son of Kareah.

hostile-officials.name: Shephatiah and Gedaliah, the officials opposing Jeremiah
hostile-officials.role: Two officials who ask the king to kill Jeremiah
hostile-officials.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hostile-officials.importance: They hear Jeremiah tell the people to go out to the Chaldeans and live. With Jucal and Pashhur, they tell the king he weakens the soldiers. The king gives Jeremiah into their hands. They lower him into a pit of mud.
hostile-officials.connections: Shephatiah is Mattan’s son. Gedaliah is Pashhur’s son, and is not Gedaliah the governor.

malchijah-royal.name: Malchijah, the king’s son
malchijah-royal.role: King’s son whose pit holds Jeremiah
malchijah-royal.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
malchijah-royal.importance: The officials throw Jeremiah into his pit in the court of the guard. The pit has no water, only mud, and Jeremiah sinks in it. Malchijah himself does nothing in the story.
malchijah-royal.connections: He is called the king’s son. The text does not say he is Pashhur’s father.

ebedmelech.name: Ebedmelech
ebedmelech.role: Ethiopian palace servant who rescues Jeremiah
ebedmelech.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ebedmelech.importance: He hears that Jeremiah is in the pit and warns the king he will die. The king gives him thirty men. He lowers old rags for Jeremiah to pad the ropes, then pulls him out. God promises Ebedmelech that he will live when the city falls.
ebedmelech.connections: He is an Ethiopian who serves in King Zedekiah’s house.

babylonian-officers.name: The Babylonian officers at Jerusalem
babylonian-officers.role: Babylonian officials who sit in the gate and free Jeremiah
babylonian-officers.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
babylonian-officers.importance: They enter Jerusalem when the wall is broken and sit in the middle gate. Later they send for Jeremiah and take him out of the court of the guard. They hand him to Gedaliah. The text does not say if the two Nergal Sharezer names are one man.
babylonian-officers.connections: Verse 3 lists Nergal Sharezer, Samgarnebo, Sarsechim, and a second Nergal Sharezer. Verse 13 names Nebushazban and Nergal Sharezer with Nebuzaradan.

nebuzaradan.name: Nebuzaradan
nebuzaradan.role: Babylonian captain who burns the city and frees Jeremiah
nebuzaradan.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nebuzaradan.importance: He burns the temple, the king’s house, and the houses of Jerusalem. He carries people to Babylon and leaves the poorest to farm. At Ramah he takes off Jeremiah’s chains and lets him choose where to go. He takes Seraiah and Zephaniah to Riblah.
nebuzaradan.connections: He is Nebuchadnezzar’s captain of the guard. He leaves the remaining people with Gedaliah.

gedaliah.name: Gedaliah, son of Ahikam
gedaliah.role: Governor placed over Judah’s remaining people
gedaliah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
gedaliah.importance: The king of Babylon makes him governor, and he lives at Mizpah. He tells the commanders to serve Babylon and gather wine, fruit, and oil. Johanan warns him about Ishmael, but he does not believe it. Ishmael kills him at a meal in Mizpah.
gedaliah.connections: He is Ahikam’s son and Shaphan’s grandson. He is not Gedaliah the son of Pashhur.

ishmael-nethaniah.name: Ishmael, son of Nethaniah
ishmael-nethaniah.role: Man of the royal family who kills Gedaliah
ishmael-nethaniah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ishmael-nethaniah.importance: He eats with Gedaliah at Mizpah, then kills him with ten men. Two days later he kills most of eighty men who come with offerings. He takes the people of Mizpah captive and heads for Ammon. Johanan catches him at Gibeon, and he escapes with eight men.
ishmael-nethaniah.connections: He is the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama. Johanan says Baalis sent him.

johanan-kareah.name: Johanan, son of Kareah
johanan-kareah.role: Commander who warns Gedaliah and later leads the people to Egypt
johanan-kareah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
johanan-kareah.importance: He tells Gedaliah that Ishmael plans to kill him and offers to kill Ishmael first. After the murder he frees Ishmael’s captives at Gibeon. He asks Jeremiah to pray, calls the answer a lie, and leads all to Egypt.
johanan-kareah.connections: He is Kareah’s son and Jonathan’s brother. He warns Gedaliah, fights Ishmael, and argues with Jeremiah.

jonathan-kareah.name: Jonathan, son of Kareah
jonathan-kareah.role: Commander named beside his brother Johanan
jonathan-kareah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jonathan-kareah.importance: He comes with his brother and the other commanders to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells them to serve the king of Babylon. The text names him only here.
jonathan-kareah.connections: He is Kareah’s son and Johanan’s brother. He is not Jonathan the scribe.

seraiah-captain.name: Seraiah, son of Tanhumeth
seraiah-captain.role: Commander who comes to Gedaliah at Mizpah
seraiah-captain.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
seraiah-captain.importance: He comes with his men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells the commanders not to fear serving the Chaldeans. The text names him only in this list.
seraiah-captain.connections: He is Tanhumeth’s son. He is not Seraiah the son of Neriah or Seraiah the chief priest.

jezaniah-maacathite.name: Jezaniah
jezaniah-maacathite.role: Commander who joins the gathering at Mizpah
jezaniah-maacathite.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jezaniah-maacathite.importance: He comes with his men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells the commanders to gather wine, summer fruits, and oil. The text names him only in this list.
jezaniah-maacathite.connections: The text calls him the son of the Maacathite. It does not link him with Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah.

baalis.name: Baalis
baalis.role: Ammonite king whom Johanan accuses of sending Ishmael
baalis.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
baalis.importance: Johanan tells Gedaliah that Baalis has sent Ishmael to kill him. Gedaliah does not believe it. The text gives only Johanan’s report. Later Ishmael does kill Gedaliah and flees toward Ammon.
baalis.connections: He is king of the children of Ammon. Johanan links him with Ishmael.

jezaniah-hoshaiah.name: Jezaniah, son of Hoshaiah
jezaniah-hoshaiah.role: Leader who asks Jeremiah to pray for the survivors
jezaniah-hoshaiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jezaniah-hoshaiah.importance: He comes with Johanan and all the people to Jeremiah. They ask him to pray that God will show them the way. They promise to obey, whether the answer is good or bad. The text does not say if he and Azariah are one man.
jezaniah-hoshaiah.connections: He is Hoshaiah’s son and stands with Johanan. Azariah in 43:2 is also called Hoshaiah’s son.

azariah-hoshaiah.name: Azariah, son of Hoshaiah
azariah-hoshaiah.role: Leader who accuses Jeremiah of lying about Egypt
azariah-hoshaiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
azariah-hoshaiah.importance: Jeremiah tells the people not to go to Egypt. Azariah tells him he speaks falsely. He says Baruch turned Jeremiah against them to hand them to the Chaldeans. The text does not say if he and Jezaniah are one man.
azariah-hoshaiah.connections: He is Hoshaiah’s son and speaks with Johanan. Jezaniah in 42:1 is also called Hoshaiah’s son.

women-queen.name: The women defending offerings to the queen
women-queen.role: Judean women in Egypt who burn incense to the queen of the sky
women-queen.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
women-queen.importance: They and their husbands tell Jeremiah they will not listen to him. They say food was plenty when they burned incense to the queen of the sky. They say hunger and the sword came when they stopped. Jeremiah answers that the incense itself brought the disaster.
women-queen.connections: They say their husbands knew of the cakes and drink offerings.

hophra.name: Pharaoh Hophra
hophra.role: Egyptian king named in Jeremiah’s warning
hophra.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hophra.importance: The people of Judah have gone to Egypt to be safe. God says he will give Hophra to enemies who seek his life. This will be the sign that God’s words against them stand.
hophra.connections: Jeremiah sets him beside Zedekiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar took.

necho.name: Pharaoh Necoh
necho.role: Egyptian king whose army is struck at Carchemish
necho.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
necho.importance: The message about Egypt opens with his army at Carchemish. Nebuchadnezzar strikes it in the fourth year of Jehoiakim. The verse says no more about Necoh himself.
necho.connections: His army faces Nebuchadnezzar by the river Euphrates.

seraiah-neriah.name: Seraiah, son of Neriah
seraiah-neriah.role: Official told to read Jeremiah’s Babylon scroll and sink it
seraiah-neriah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
seraiah-neriah.importance: He goes with King Zedekiah to Babylon in the king’s fourth year. Jeremiah gives him a scroll of all the evil coming on Babylon. He must read it there and tie a stone to it. Then he must throw it in the Euphrates. He must say that Babylon will sink the same way.
seraiah-neriah.connections: He is the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah. Baruch is called by the same father and grandfather.

hamutal.name: Hamutal
hamutal.role: Zedekiah’s mother, named in the last chapter
hamutal.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hamutal.importance: The last chapter names her when it tells of Zedekiah’s reign. Her father is Jeremiah of Libnah. The prophet Jeremiah is from Anathoth, not Libnah. She does nothing in the story.
hamutal.connections: She is Zedekiah’s mother and the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

seraiah-priest.name: Seraiah, the chief priest
seraiah-priest.role: Chief priest taken and killed after Jerusalem falls
seraiah-priest.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
seraiah-priest.importance: Nebuzaradan takes him from the city with Zephaniah and three keepers of the threshold. He brings them to the king of Babylon at Riblah. The king puts them to death there.
seraiah-priest.connections: Nebuzaradan takes him with Zephaniah the second priest. He is not Seraiah the son of Neriah.

solomon.name: Solomon
solomon.role: Earlier king who made the temple’s bronze pieces
solomon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
solomon.importance: The Chaldeans break up the bronze pillars, the sea, and the twelve bronze bulls. They carry the bronze to Babylon. The text says King Solomon had made these things. He does nothing else in this book.
solomon.connections: The text says King Solomon made them for the LORD’s house.

evil-merodach.name: Evilmerodach
evil-merodach.role: Babylonian king who releases Jehoiachin from prison
evil-merodach.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
evil-merodach.importance: In his first year he lets Jehoiachin out of prison. He speaks kindly to him and gives him a seat above the other captive kings. He changes his prison clothes. He gives him food every day for the rest of his life.
evil-merodach.connections: He is king of Babylon and deals kindly with Jehoiachin.
